out.other_title: Self-critiquing models: model-written critiques help humans find flaws in summaries
out.rationale: Bowman et al. say their result shows, echoing Saunders et al., that present large language models can help humans achieve difficult tasks, so both ask whether model assistance helps humans, in different settings, and the multiple-choice QA result is not evidence for Saunders et al.'s summary-critique claim. The tasks differ: Saunders et al. use model-written critiques to help humans find flaws in summaries, while Bowman et al. use LLM assistance on multiple-choice QA. Saunders et al.'s critique models are fine-tuned by behavioural cloning, while Bowman et al. use present large language models in a simple proof-of-concept sandwiching experiment.
